rows: In the **customers** dataset, **6 rows** have been quarantined under rule **notes_no_card_number** because free-text notes fields contain what appears to be raw payment card numbers (sample customer IDs: c_00729, c_00887, c_00971, c_01653, c_01834).

The most likely cause is that customer service agents or an intake form are inadvertently capturing card numbers in an unstructured notes/comments field rather than routing them through the secure, tokenised payment capture flow.

Implement a real-time PAN-detection regex mask on all free-text input fields at the point of entry, automatically redact or reject any value matching a card-number pattern, and retrain agents to use the designated secure payment capture tool instead of notes fields.

11 rows in the payments dataset have been quarantined under rule amount_positive because the amount field contains negative values (e.g., -101.45, -7.30, -88.60, -36.72, -224.90 SGD), violating the expectation that payment amounts must be greater than zero.

The negative amounts were most likely introduced by an upstream system recording refunds, reversals, or credit adjustments using the same payments transaction file rather than a dedicated offsetting ledger or separate transaction type.

Introduce a transaction_type field (e.g., PAYMENT, REFUND, REVERSAL) to distinguish negative-value entries, route non-payment transaction types to their own pipeline, and enforce the amount_positive rule exclusively on rows where transaction_type is PAYMENT; additionally, flag the one row missing merchant_id for a separate completeness check.

50 rows in the payments dataset were quarantined by the amount_present rule because the amount field is missing from the main schema and instead appears embedded as a string (e.g., "22.22 SGD") inside the rescued column, sourced from payments_drift.json.

The source file payments_drift.json contains the amount value combined with the currency code as a single string in a non-standard field, causing the pipeline's schema mapping to fail to populate the dedicated amount column and triggering the amount_present rule.

Update the ingestion pipeline to parse the rescued column for these records, splitting the combined amount-currency string to extract the numeric amount and populate the amount field correctly, or enforce a schema contract on payments_drift.json upstream so that amount is delivered as a standalone numeric field.

12 rows in the payments dataset have been quarantined under rule currency_valid because they contain invalid ISO 4217 currency codes — predominantly "SGX" (not a recognised currency code) and "VND" appearing in contexts that may indicate a mapping error.

The most likely cause is a data-entry or upstream system mapping error where "SGX" was mistakenly used instead of the valid Singapore Dollar code "SGD", possibly due to confusion with the SGX stock exchange ticker or a misconfigured currency lookup table.

Audit and correct the currency code mapping in the upstream source system or ETL pipeline — replacing "SGX" with "SGD" where appropriate — and add a validation step that rejects any currency code not present in the ISO 4217 reference list before records are ingested.
14 rows in the payments dataset have been quarantined because the merchant_id field is null, violating the merchant_id_not_null rule across transactions in SGD and MYR currencies.

The merchant_id is likely missing due to an upstream ingestion or integration failure — such as a payment processor webhook or API response omitting the merchant identifier when a transaction is initiated without a fully registered or matched merchant account.

Enforce a NOT NULL constraint and mandatory validation on merchant_id at the point of ingestion, and implement a lookup or enrichment step to back-fill merchant_id from a reference table before records enter the payments dataset.
